This commit implements the delayed release logic for bpf_list_push_front
and bpf_list_push_back.
Once a node has been added to the list
PTR_UNTRUSTED. However
column2: it is only released once the lock protecting the

column1: list is unlocked. For such PTR_TO_BTF_ID | MEM_ALLOC with PTR_UNTRUSTED
set but an active ref_obj_id
column2: it is still permitted to read them as long

column1: as the lock is held. Writing to them is not allowed.
This allows having read access to push items we no longer own until we
release the lock guarding the list
when working with these APIs.
Note that enabling write support has fairly tricky interactions with
what happens inside the critical section. Just as an example
bpf_obj_drop is not permitted
the PTR_UNTRUSTED pointer while the object gets released back to the
memory allocator would violate safety properties we wish to guarantee
(i.e. not crashing the kernel). The memory could be reused for a
different type in the BPF program or even in the kernel as it gets
eventually kfree'd.
Not enabling bpf_obj_drop inside the critical section would appear to
prevent all of the above
column2: but that is more of an artifical limitation

column1: right now. Since the write support is tangled with how we handle
potential aliasing of nodes inside the critical section that may or may
not be part of the list anymore
column2: it has been deferred to a future patch.
